brief.analysis: This looks stretched only against a flat 5-year average; measured against defense's own steadily rising trend it is barely extended, and those two readings openly disagree — direct evidence the average itself is climbing, not that price is dislocated. There is no moving-average confirmation, the uptrend is still intact, and the forward hit rate is weak (three of seven). Rising NATO and global defense budgets are a structural rerating: this is a mean that has moved, not a rubber band.
brief.report_line: We would avoid shorting defense versus the S&P: the apparent richness disappears once you account for defense's own rising trend, and structurally higher global defense budgets mean the old average has simply moved up rather than the pair being dislocated.

brief.analysis: The trade is already mostly over — gold has snapped back toward stocks, the 200-day-average target is met, and measured against gold's own rising path it is no longer stretched (its trend-relative reading is slightly cheap, not rich). The strongest regime argument is that persistent central-bank gold buying has structurally lifted gold's value, so the flat 5-year average target another 11% lower is chasing a mean that has drifted upward. Take what reversion is left but do not press toward the old flat mean.
brief.report_line: We are short gold versus U.S. equities with most of the reversion already banked; the key risk is that steady central-bank gold buying has permanently raised gold's floor, making the remaining 11% downside to the old average an unreliable target.

brief.analysis: Semiconductors are still meaningfully rich versus the broader Nasdaq, and crucially they remain stretched even when measured against their own steeply rising trend — this is genuine over-extension, not just a drifting average. But the driver is the AI build-out, a live structural theme, and the flat 5-year average target sits an implausible 68% away, so only the 200-day-average target (~14%) is credible. Trade it small toward that nearer target, not the old mean.
brief.report_line: We are short semiconductors versus the Nasdaq on genuine over-extension, but sized down: the AI capital-spending cycle is a live structural force, so we target only the 200-day average and treat the far-lower 5-year mean as invalid.

brief.analysis: Metals and mining ran far ahead of the market and have already reverted to the 200-day average with the fifty-day trend rolling over, so the near-term snap-back is real and partly banked. Two cautions temper it: the forward evidence rests on just two past episodes, and the same silver/copper structural-demand forces flagged elsewhere argue the flat 5-year average a further 21% lower is a suspect target. Take the confirmed reversion in small size and do not chase toward the old mean.
brief.report_line: We are short metals-and-mining versus the S&P on a confirmed pullback to the 200-day average, sized down because the evidence base is thin and the same commodity-demand story that lifted the group makes the deeper 5-year target unreliable.

brief.analysis: Silver ran enormously far ahead of gold and has already reverted most of the way, with full moving-average confirmation and the 200-day-average target achieved — a textbook rubber-band snap that is playing out cleanly. The regime caveat is silver's real industrial-demand and supply-deficit story, which argues the flat 5-year average a further 18% away may be too low a target. The near-term reversion is clean and confirmed, so act, but treat the 200-day level as the objective rather than the old mean.
brief.report_line: We are short silver versus gold after an extreme run that is reverting cleanly with full trend confirmation; the residual risk is silver's structural industrial-demand story, so we anchor to the 200-day average rather than the deeper 5-year mean.
